Releases are cut by pushing a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`, for example `v2026.09.2`. This comes from a project memory in EngramDB. The repo has no release docs, CI workflow files or release Makefile target to check it against.

1. Make sure `main` has the commits you want to ship. Run `make test` first (the full suite, including the Postgres tests). `make test-fast` skips the Postgres tests.
2. Pick the tag: the current year and month, then `N`, a counter for that month. I'm assuming it starts at 1 and goes up with each release, but the memory doesn't say. Check the existing tags with `git tag -l 'v2026.10.*'` to find the next number.
3. Create and push the tag, for example `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`.
4. CI builds and publishes from the tag. Never publish by hand.

I couldn't find the CI config in this checkout, so I can't say what the pipeline does or how to check that it succeeded. I haven't created or pushed any tag.
